from the national synodal assembly in answer to the question, “what does god want of the church at this time?”, t he proposals suggest at first glance what god m ight be asking us to do. but there is something else! they are also pointing to what god might be asking us to be. or what god might be asking us to become. actions can too easily be put in a corner and be seen as the responsibility of someone else. but becoming is something that belongs to us all. it’s about our shared identity – not just about what we do, but who we are. it’s about growth. it’s about conversion. it’s about becoming the people that god wants us to be. actions can be decided, implemented, and completed. but growth, change, conversion, becoming – are a journey over time. a journey of becoming a church that proclaims the gospel a church that is a community of belonging a church that is a place of healing a church that accompanies a church that empowers for ministry and co-responsibility. the proposals now find their place in a vision of the church that we are seeking to become. and we can all find ourselves in this vision of the church. the pathways offer a real alternative to the polarised and polarising discourse that characterises so much of the life of our church and our w orld. they offer us a way of being together. and long after recommendations from today have been decided, implemented, evaluated, the p athways will continue to offer us ways of becoming, ways of finding our identity, and ways of walking the path together. fr. declan hurley , national synodal assembly ,
